claim.quote: The mass of the top quark is measured to be m_top = 172.08 +/- 0.39 (stat) +/- 0.82 (syst) GeV.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Eur. Phys. J. C 79, 290 (2019).

key_value.quote: The mass of the top quark is measured to be m_top = 172.08 +/- 0.39 (stat) +/- 0.82 (syst) GeV.

name: Measurement of the top quark mass

significance.note: A measurement, not a discovery; no significance is quoted.

summary.plain: ATLAS measured the mass of the top quark, one of the fundamental particles of the Standard Model, using 8 TeV collision data, and combined the result with its earlier top-quark mass measurements.
summary.technical: Lepton+jets tt̄ candidates from 20.2 fb⁻¹ of 8 TeV data, three-dimensional template method: m_top = 172.08 ± 0.39 (stat) ± 0.82 (syst) GeV; a combination with previous ATLAS m_top measurements gives m_top = 172.69 ± 0.25 (stat) ± 0.41 (syst) GeV.

title: Measurement of the top quark mass in the ttbar -> lepton+jets channel from sqrt(s)=8 TeV ATLAS data and combination with previous results
why_it_matters: The top-quark mass enters the electroweak fit and the calculation of the stability of the Higgs potential, so sharper top-mass measurements sharpen Standard Model consistency tests.
